description: The P1 message contract of the standalone FOP ledger. Two independent readers (tests/cost_basis_fop_contract_test.py and tests/cost_basis_fop_identity.test.js) validate every example against these types and must agree: each valid example passes, each invalid one fails with the expected path and code. A client can build a legal request from this file alone: the types fix every message shape, "formats" fixes the text forms, and "domainRules" lists the cross-field checks the server makes (cost_basis_fop_domain.py, P2) that the schema language cannot express; "domainCases" works those rules through with stored and incoming rows and the outcome P2 must give.

schemaLanguage.ref: {"ref": Type} uses a named type; "nullable": true on any spec also accepts null.
schemaLanguage.integer: an integral number; min, max, nonzero.
schemaLanguage.number: a finite number; min, exclusiveMin (reported as min), nonzero.
schemaLanguage.map: a JSON object with free-text keys whose every value matches "values"; minEntries. An entry is reported at path.key.
schemaLanguage.object: fields, required; a field not listed is "additional". Nullable fields are still required: absent and null are different.
schemaLanguage.variant: an object chosen by the value of field "on" among "cases"; an unknown value is "variant".
schemaLanguage.rules: on objects, after the fields: when {field, in}; require (present and not null); forbid (absent or null); sign {field: positive|negative}; exactlyOne [fields]; equals {field, negate: other} (field = -other, 1e-9); lessOrEqual [a, b] (both present and well formed; string order, allowed only between two fields of one fixed-width type, IsoDate or UtcInstant, where string order is time order). A broken rule is reported at the object as "rule:<id>".
schemaLanguage.paths: dot-separated field names with [index] for array items; "" is the root.
schemaLanguage.codes: missing, additional, type, null, enum, pattern, minLength, min, max, nonzero, const, minItems, maxItems, minEntries, variant, rule:<id>.

formats.IsoDate: YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar or exchange trade date; always 10 characters.
formats.UtcInstant: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ in UTC, always six fractional digits and 27 characters, so text order is time order in both readers and in SQLite. Every economic or evidence time uses it: executions, ranges, baselines, observations and as-of instants. It keeps every digit its source gave and pads the rest with zeros; nothing is rounded or truncated, so a fill at 14:30:05.900 is after an as-of of 14:30:05.000000. A source more precise than a microsecond is not cut either: it becomes a TimeRange from the microsecond below to the one above (plan §9.2). An instant is as precise as its source; time.sourceTimeText keeps the original text, and fills a source puts in the same instant are ordered by time.orderEvidence.
formats.RecordedAtUtc: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, 20 characters: when the server wrote a row, in the form cost_basis_store already stamps createdAtUtc, updatedAtUtc, archivedAtUtc and voidedAtUtc. Bookkeeping only: never an economic time and never compared with a UtcInstant.

domainRules.rule: Every write except create_cost_basis_book carries requestId, bookId, bookIdentity and expectedLedgerVersion. The server compares identity and version with the stored ledger before anything else and refuses a difference with ledger_changed (plan §8.3). Append, void and metadata commits are idempotent on clientToken; an import on importBatchId and clientTokenPrefix.
contractRef, deliveredContractRef and bindingRef name a record of the same package or one already stored for the book, at exactly that revision (plan §4.3, §8.1).

An option_assignment or option_exercise references a resolved binding (verified_broker, verified_statement or manual_attested) whose optionContractId is the contract of its contractRef and whose futureContractId is the contract of its deliveredContractRef (plan §4.3, §6.1).

packageKey labels an event inside one package, is unique there and is never stored. A fee's feeSource names its source event exactly once: by eventId, a live event of the book that is not a fee, or by packageKey, an event of the same package that is not a fee. The server resolves a packageKey to the new or matched stored event id in the same transaction and stores only that id, so a fee and its trade can arrive in one import (plan §13.2).
Every events[*].sources[*] names one fopPackage.sourceRecords entry by namespace and sourceRef. Allocation (role, quantity, fees) lives on the event side; the record holds the row itself.
Every sourceRecords entry is allocated by at least one event of the same package, and no two entries share namespace and sourceRef.

Over one record, the sum of |allocated quantity| is at most |statedQuantity| and the sum of allocated fees at most |statedFees|, where stated. Allocations are evidence and never enter an economic sum (plan §8.1).
Every sourceRecords[*].account and every event account equal bookIdentity.account; a masked statement.account must be one the user confirmed for that account (plan §9.1).

A package with a flex_trade, ib_exec or activity_row record is an ImportRequest with a non-null statement, and every such record has the statement's format: one file per import. An AppendRequest carries tws_exec records only, or none.

A record whose account, namespace and sourceRef are already stored for the book is the same reference, and the server compares its economic content with the stored one: the record's statedQuantity and statedFees and, for each event it is allocated to, the kind, contracts, futureContracts, price, cashAmount, fees, includeInCost, openClose, feeCategory, feeIsRefund, adjustmentScope, baselineKind and baselineAsOfUtc; the contract terms behind contractRef and deliveredContractRef (not record ids, revisions or evidence fields); the binding by what it binds, which delivery_follows_binding makes that same contractRef -> deliveredContractRef pair, never by binding id or revision; the fee source by the event it resolves to (a stored event id, or the stored event its in-package source matched); the time facts exchangeTradeDate, executedAtUtc, timeRange and orderEvidence; and the allocation's role, quantity and fees. These fields are compared whenever they apply to the event kind: a change in fee ownership, cycle attribution, inclusion, open/close intent, baseline interpretation or delivered contract is an economic revision even if quantities and cash are unchanged. Event account is validated against the book/source identity; source, externalRef and packageKey are provenance, and note alone is non-economic. Every event field and time fact has exactly one comparison policy; a new one cannot be silently ignored. Equal content is a duplicate: the import reports it and neither stores nor allocates it again. Any difference is a revision of the same reference: the whole import fails with import_revision_conflict, naming the reference and every differing field, and nothing is skipped (plan §9.1). Differences that do not decide it are reported: raw fields outside that content (a description, a new column), sourceTimeText and sourceTimezone (the same instant written another way), and a binding revision with the same delivery, whose adoption is a metadata commit, never an import side effect (plan §4.3). A correction is a void or an archived rebuild (plan §9.4), and a void keeps its sources consumed (plan §8.3). domainCases works this rule through.
An opening_balance with baselineKind unknown_cost references a FOP contract. A FUT baseline needs a trade cost or a reference price (plan §9.2).
